name: Run Control
description: Horizontal locomotion for a side-view body: accelerate toward the input direction, decelerate to a stop when it is released, and turn around faster than you accelerate from rest. It owns horizontal velocity outright, which is why airControlFraction lives here rather than on movement.jump_core — whoever owns the velocity has to apply the multiplier, and splitting the two across components means one of them writing into the other's state. Distinct from movement.basic_walk, which declares no deceleration and is written for a body with no gravity axis; the two are alternatives, not companions. It emits nothing on purpose: movement.started already has an emitter and three listeners, and a second source would deliver every one of them twice.

implementations.note: Implemented in the consuming application; not verifiable from this repository.

inputs.name: maxRunSpeed
inputs.description: Top horizontal speed in world units per second.

inputs.name: groundAcceleration
inputs.description: How hard the body accelerates toward the input direction while grounded. At the defaults top speed arrives in about a tenth of a second, which reads as responsive; a tenth of this reads as ice.

inputs.name: groundDeceleration
inputs.description: How hard it slows when input is released. Below groundAcceleration by default, so stopping is slightly softer than starting.

inputs.name: airControlFraction
inputs.description: Fraction of ground acceleration available while airborne. 0 is a committed jump aimed entirely at takeoff; 1 is full mid-air redirection. The single knob that most decides whether a jump feels heavy or floaty.

inputs.name: turnAroundMultiplier
inputs.description: Extra acceleration applied when input opposes current velocity. Without it a reversal has to bleed off the old speed at deceleration rate before building the new one, which reads as the character ignoring the stick.

outputs.name: facing
outputs.description: -1 or 1. Holds the last non-zero direction after input stops, so a standing character still faces where it was going.
